paper.title: Validity, Sparse Holes, and Breadth in Language Generation: Banach Density, Topology, and Geometry
paper.summary: Studies validity, sparse holes, and breadth through lower Banach density, containment topology, finite Cantor--Bendixson rank, and finite-tree geometry.

formalization_scope.summary: The complete selected-result inventory covers the four headline Banach-density and geometry theorems, the f-window dichotomy, the higher-dimensional discrepancy ingredient, and the principal structural claims. The structural density, topology, finite-rank, and finite-tree results are proved at their stated interfaces. Theorem 5.8 gives the sharp centered-cube half-density guarantee. Overview 2.2 and Corollaries 4.2–4.3 are proved using a periodic hard family. Overview 2.4 and detailed Theorem 5.1 hold on the same injective enumeration under both printed growth premises. The sharp finite-rank Theorem 4.5 and its window-bound and reordering corollaries have a separate finite-history proof. Theorem 5.9 has a counterexample on a valid printed tier and a full lattice-site-length repair with the same numerical discrepancy constants.
specializations: One-dimensional densities are valued in extended nonnegative reals so nested infima are total.
Cantor--Bendixson ranks are formalized only at finite natural-number levels.
Claim 4.20 uses Mathlib predecessor-tree assumptions that make ancestor chains comparable.

Separate Lean replay of the later finite-rank theorem gives 5.5 and 5.6 on unrestricted targets and locations for every filter eventually dominating a fixed positive power of log V. Taking exponent one gives the fixed-shape density clause of 5.7.
gaps: Detailed 4.1 has a proved ambient-coordinate version and a counterexample under the target-rank convention.

The filtered-rectangle generation guarantee 5.5 remains open. The geometric-length coloring bound 5.9 is false even on a valid tier. Its lattice-site-length correction is proved. The exact-identification reading of Corollary 5.7 has a finite-rank counterexample.

claims.title: Lower Banach density is the smallest lower window density
claims.statement_summary: For every admissible nondecreasing window bound f, the one-dimensional lower Banach density is at most the corresponding lower f-window density.

formalization.notes: Lean packages the source inequality as the equivalent identity saying that lower Banach density is the infimum over admissible bounds, attained by the constant-top bound.

claims.title: Every unbounded window scale has a countable zero-density hard class
claims.statement_summary: For every unbounded window function f, there is a countable language collection for which every valid generator has lower f-window density zero on some target; the result yields the Banach-density and finite-output-speed corollaries.

source_assessment.notes: The detailed proof ends on the full natural-number target. At the admissible unbounded scale 1+floor(k/8), P39 gives a strictly positive lower bound for every presentation of that target, contradicting this diagonal. The same obstruction applies on every target if windows use target ranks. Overview 2.2 and Corollary 4.2 only ask for unrestricted Banach density. With ambient positions and a target-count denominator, the zero bound on a sparse target has a separate proof by stretching the positions in a periodic family.

formalization.notes: Overview 2.2 and Corollaries 4.2–4.3 hold on ℕ. For unbounded f a sparse target proves the ambient-coordinate, target-count formulation. The source diagonal on ℕ fails, and the target-rank formulation has a counterexample for a linear f.

claims.title: Filtered higher-dimensional generation attains one half at finite rank
claims.statement_summary: Overview Theorem 2.5 asks for one generator handling every nondegenerate rectangle sequence, with a divergent multiplier chosen per sequence in equation (2). Theorem 5.5 first fixes a nondecreasing divergent filter and a positive tolerance, then asserts that a finite-rank countable family admits a generator with filtered rectangular lower density at least one half minus the tolerance. Corollary 5.6 restricts to translated cubes. Corollary 5.7 uses fixed shapes and additionally claims exact identification.

source_assessment.notes: The source later calls 5.5 Theorem 5.6 and 5.7 says identifies in the generation discussion. Equation (28) also has a four-point counterexample. Opposite-color pairs can cross the boundary of the measured rectangle even for a unique closest partner. The existence theorem remains open. Taken literally, the identification conclusion of Corollary 5.7 fails even on exact injective texts for the rank-two class consisting of the full universe and its co-singletons. The discrepancy-one strip coloring gives 2n inputs and zero replies in a rectangle of area 30n under the unique nearest-opposite-color rule.

formalization.notes: The unrestricted higher-dimensional generator existence claims in 2.5, 5.5 and 5.6 remain unproved here. We have no counterexample to those existence claims. RectanglePairingCheck.lean verifies a counterexample to the within-rectangle pairing estimate (28) used in the source proof. IdentificationCheck.lean refutes the additional exact-identification conclusion of 5.7. StripPairing.lean verifies arbitrarily large fixed-phase violations with linear input excess. The static filtered half split and a causal finite-board discrepancy bound have Lean proofs. The finite-board estimate depends on board size. It does not give the required bound in terms of each rectangle’s own volume. The full finite-rank generation conclusion is proved for a family supported on a common monotone lattice chain, simultaneously for all growing filters and with bound one half. There is now a valid online generator for arbitrary finite-rank families with uniform count error q times target count plus η times geometric volume plus a presentation-dependent constant, for every positive q and η with q ≤ 1/2. This yields the headline bound under a positive occupancy floor on cofinal tests. Positive occupancy measured on a common stretched coordinate grid also gives the stronger unfiltered conclusion on large target traces. Exact half also holds on supports with logarithmically many coordinatewise ordered rows per rectangle, including arbitrary finite-rank subfamilies on planar rows whose heights at least double. The separately replayable External/Paper23PowerFilter.lean proof establishes the rectangular and translated-cube conclusions on arbitrary finite-rank families whenever the filter eventually dominates a fixed positive power of log V. It also proves the density clause of 5.7 by taking exponent one. Its fifteen pinned upstream modules and the bridge are checked with the project toolchain.

claims.title: Multi-level size-sensitive discrepancy for axis-parallel rectangles
claims.statement_summary: For every possibly infinite point set in the integer lattice, epsilon in (0,1), and positive filtration exponent, there is one global two-coloring whose discrepancy on every axis-parallel rectangle obeys the theorem's simultaneous size- and sparsity-tier bound.

source_assessment.notes: The printed tier misses dense rectangles and its capacity estimate (21) fails. Even on a valid tier-zero closed unit box the discrepancy inequality itself is false. In dimension 255 let P be the 255 coordinate vectors and α=510, ε=π/√192. Then c₀=128. Every coloring has 128 vectors of one color. Integer unit intervals in each coordinate select exactly those 128 vectors. Their discrepancy is 128 and the printed threshold is strictly smaller.

formalization.notes: Lean refutes the geometric-side-length inequality. Corrected Theorem 5.9 uses the largest number of lattice sites on a side and assigns dense overflow to the least nonnegative tier. It proves simultaneous coloring of every trace of arbitrary P with the published numerical constants. Appendix 7.4, the Hoeffding bound, quantitative neighbor summation, and compactness are proved.

lean_links.notes: The auxiliary Appendix Theorem 7.4 is fully proved. This entry contributes to the proof route for 5.9.
The counterexample uses strictly positive geometric side lengths, a valid original tier, and the exact published constants.
All point sets, including infinite sets, admit one simultaneous coloring. The normalization counts lattice sites along a side and includes dense overflow in tier zero.

relations.notes: The coloring theorem is the principal combinatorial ingredient of the filtered higher-dimensional generation result.
